the_crux_required_versus_permitted.problem: CONTIGUOUS is fundamentally about STORAGE LAYOUT, and this project holds that layout, addresses and allocation mechanism are NOT observable. The only legitimate oracle is IS_CONTIGUOUS, and only where the standard REQUIRES a given result. Where the standard merely PERMITS a processor to lay something out contiguously, asserting either value would be wrong, because a conforming processor could report either.
the_crux_required_versus_permitted.oracle_basis: 16.9.115 p5: 'The result has the value true if ARRAY has rank zero or is contiguous, and false otherwise.'

the_false_weakness_addressed.problem: .FALSE. is a DEFAULT-EQUIVALENT value - a zero-filled logical reads false - so a negative facet asserting IS_CONTIGUOUS is .FALSE. is weak on its own, because a program that never established the property would also report false.
the_false_weakness_addressed.mitigation: Both negative fixtures carry same-program .TRUE. controls.
the_false_weakness_addressed.reviewer_verification: Confirmed the controls exist AND execute before completion, so each program demonstrably distinguishes the two states rather than always reporting false.

over_suppression_check.principle: An unobservability claim that is too broad is itself a defect.
over_suppression_check.pending: 11 effect facets and 5 restriction facets remain.
over_suppression_check.reviewer_verdict: Deferral is correct. Layout, addresses, padding, copy strategy, timing and the p4 residuals are genuinely unobservable. The S8.5.7-002 restriction facets lack a required portable diagnostic, so they cannot carry a diagnostic expectation - a facet may do so only if the unit actually prohibits something, a processor is required to reject, and a single-image program can portably observe it.
over_suppression_check.conclusion: Nothing IS_CONTIGUOUS could legitimately settle was left pending out of convenience.

integrator_corrective_action.issue: The full gate failed with three failures in PRE-EXISTING sibling modules - test_contiguous_property_fixtures, test_contiguous_dummy_effect_fixtures and test_contiguous_eligibility_fixtures - each asserting an exact rendering of doc/fortran_2023_8_5_7.md. The on-disk view said 'Source review: stale' while the catalogue, after the integrator recorded the review, said 'reviewed'.
integrator_corrective_action.root_cause: THREE generators write the same view file: generate_contiguous_property_fixtures.py, generate_contiguous_dummy_effect_fixtures.py and generate_contiguous_eligibility_fixtures.py. The author emitted the view during authoring, when the catalogue was necessarily stale because authors cannot record reviews. Recording the review at integration flipped the catalogue to reviewed, leaving the rendered artefact inconsistent with it.
integrator_corrective_action.chicken_and_egg: Re-running a generator to refresh the view REWRITES the catalogue and therefore RE-STALES its content-bound review, so the view renders 'stale' again. The correct order is generator -> record review -> correct the rendered line, which is the render-after-record rule first recorded at batch130.
integrator_corrective_action.remedy: Regenerated the shared view, re-recorded the 8.5.7 catalogue review after the generator had rewritten the catalogue, then corrected the rendered review line to 'reviewed' to match the catalogue. The three sibling modules then pass, 41 tests OK.
integrator_corrective_action.generalisation: Shared view files are now known in two places: 7.5.10 has two generators and 8.5.7 has three. A fixture packet touching such a section must expect sibling modules to assert the shared rendering, and the integrator must refresh the view AFTER recording the review.
integrator_corrective_action.verification: test_contiguous_property_fixtures, test_contiguous_dummy_effect_fixtures and test_contiguous_eligibility_fixtures run 41 tests OK, and the full gate was re-run.
